definition: Datagen was a multinational software company founded in 2018 by Ofir Chakon and Gil Elbaz.
details: The company provides a platform for generating synthetic data for virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), computer vision (CV), and artificial intelligence (AI), namely, self-driving cars, robotics and IoT security.

explainer.lead: Datagen was a software company that built a platform for creating synthetic data: artificially generated examples used to develop AI and computer-vision systems. Its work mattered for areas such as self-driving cars, robotics, virtual and augmented reality, and IoT security, where useful training examples can be difficult to gather from the real world.

tiers.eli5: Imagine teaching a computer to recognize things by showing it lots of practice pictures. Instead of taking every picture with a real camera, Datagen's platform could make artificial ones on a computer. This gave people building things like self-driving cars and robots another way to create practice material.
tiers.practitioner: An engineering team could use Datagen's platform to generate synthetic examples for computer-vision or AI development rather than relying entirely on collected real-world data. The platform targeted applications including autonomous driving, robotics, VR, AR, and IoT security. Synthetic examples still need to be checked against the conditions the finished system will encounter.
tiers.paperLevel: Datagen was a company whose platform produced synthetic data: samples generated artificially rather than collected directly from real-world observations. Its stated application domains were VR, AR, computer vision, and AI, including self-driving cars, robotics, and IoT security. No formal data-generation model or evaluation results are specified.

explainer.example: A team developing a self-driving car could use Datagen's platform to create artificial driving examples, then use those examples alongside other data while developing the car's computer-vision system.
